key_insight: They formalize an end-to-end, composable security proof for entanglement-based qubit BB84 in Lean, removing hidden assumptions and strengthening trust in quantum cryptography arguments.
engineering_relevance: This shows that theorem provers can both verify critical security protocols and help improve them, making formal methods a practical tool for quantum communication design.
method: Built the security proof in Lean using only the standard axioms and explicit local-operations/classical-communication structure.
Applied the postselection technique to prove composable security against coherent attacks with finite-size effects.
Used an LLM-based autoformalization pipeline to accelerate proof construction and then reuse it for discovery.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a completed Lean formalization of BB84 security plus a follow-on use of the same pipeline to reduce the finite-size key-rate penalty.
watch_item: The result depends on the fidelity of the autoformalized specification and the proof assumptions encoded in Lean, so protocol-to-code translation remains a careful implementation step.
paper_title: Quantum Cryptography and Autoformalization in Lean
